To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we can improve the sample efficiency of reinforcement learning in certain resource allocation problems by using a form of multi task learning that exploits an invariance between the tasks, which we call permutation invariance multi task learning, or PIMTL.

(i) we propose a novel approach to multi-task reinforcement learning, which is motivated by a theoretical performance bound and (ii) we show that this approach is highly sample efficient in two challenging real-world sequential resource optimization problems, where this invariant property is present: portfolio optimization and meta learning in federated learning.

We introduce a multi-task learning setting where the tasks share a permutation invariant structure, and show that this can be exploited to improve the sample efficiency of reinforcement learning in these settings.
